questions.stem: Convert the truth table for the function F(A,B,C) into sum of products (SOP) form.
questions.solution: The SOP form of F(A, B, C) is (A'+B+C)(A+B'+C). This expression represents all input combinations that result in an output of 1.
questions.explanation: To convert a truth table to SOP, identify groups of inputs that produce 0 and negate them. The negated groups are then ANDed together. In this case, the groups producing 0 are A=0, B=0, C=1 and A=0, B=1, C=0. Negating these groups gives us (A'+B+C) and (A+B'+C), which when ANDed give the SOP form.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Not negating the input combinations that produce 0. This results in an incorrect SOP form.

questions.stem: Express the function G(X, Y, Z) = XYZ + X'YZ' + XY'Z using sum of products (SOP).
questions.solution: The SOP form of G(X, Y, Z) is (X+Y+Z')(X+Y'+Z). This expression represents all the input combinations that result in an output of 1.
questions.explanation: To convert a given product of sums to SOP, distribute each term over the other terms. In this case, we have XYZ + X'YZ' + XY'Z = (X(YZ) + X'(YZ')) + XY'(Z) = (X+Y'+Z')(X+Y+Z)
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Incorrect distribution of terms. This leads to extra or missing terms in the SOP form.

questions.stem: Convert the function H(A, B, C, D) = ABC'D + A'BCD into sum of products (SOP).
questions.solution: The SOP form of H(A, B, C, D) is (A'+B+CD')(A+B'D). This expression represents all the input combinations that result in an output of 1.
questions.explanation: To convert a given function to SOP, distribute each term over the other terms. In this case, we have ABC'D + A'BCD = (A(BC'D) + A'(BCD)) = (A'+B+CD')(A+B'D)
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Not distributing all terms properly. This results in an incorrect SOP form.

questions.stem: Express the truth table for the function I(W, X, Y) using sum of products (SOP).
questions.solution: The SOP form of I(W, X, Y) is (W+X'+Y')(W+X+Y). This expression represents all the input combinations that result in an output of 1.
questions.explanation: To convert a truth table to SOP, identify groups of inputs that produce 0 and negate them. The negated groups are then ANDed together. In this case, the group producing 0 is W=0, X=1, Y=0. Negating this group gives us (W+X'+Y'), which when combined with all other input combinations in SOP form gives (W+X+Y)(W+X'+Y')
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Not considering all input combinations that produce 0. This leads to an incomplete SOP form.

questions.stem: Convert the function J(U, V, W) = U'VW + UV'W into sum of products (SOP).
questions.solution: The SOP form of J(U, V, W) is (U+V+W')(U+V'+W). This expression represents all the input combinations that result in an output of 1.
questions.explanation: To convert a given product of sums to SOP, distribute each term over the other terms. In this case, we have U'VW + UV'W = (U'(VW) + U(V'W)) = (U+V+W')(U+V'+W)
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Incorrect distribution of terms. This leads to extra or missing terms in the SOP form.

questions.stem: Express the truth table for the function K(M, N, O) using sum of products (SOP).
questions.solution: The SOP form of K(M, N, O) is (M+N+O')(M+N'+O). This expression represents all the input combinations that result in an output of 1.
questions.explanation: To convert a truth table to SOP, identify groups of inputs that produce 0 and negate them. The negated groups are then ANDed together. In this case, there is no group producing 0, so the SOP form is simply (M+N+O')(M+N'+O)
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Assuming a group with all inputs set to 0 exists when it does not. This results in an unnecessary negation and incorrect SOP form.

questions.stem: Convert the function L(P, Q, R) = PQR + P'QR' into sum of products (SOP).
questions.solution: The SOP form of L(P, Q, R) is (P+Q+R')(P+Q'+R). This expression represents all the input combinations that result in an output of 1.
questions.explanation: To convert a given product of sums to SOP, distribute each term over the other terms. In this case, we have PQR + P'QR' = (P(QR) + P'(QR')) = (P+Q+R')(P+Q'+R)
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Incorrect distribution of terms. This leads to extra or missing terms in the SOP form.
